name: Genetic Complex Vascular Malformation with Associated Anomalies
aliases: Hereditary Complex Vascular Anomaly with Multisystem Involvement

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Genetic Complex Vascular Malformation Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of multifocal complex vascular malformations involving capillary, venous, and lymphatic vessels
Congenital anomalies affecting musculoskeletal or neurological systems such as limb hypertrophy or cerebral malformations
Identification of pathogenic variant in genes known to cause complex vascular malformations (e.g., RASA1, EPHB4)
Radiologic evidence of combined vascular malformations on MRI, ultrasound, or angiography
Positive family history of similar vascular anomalies or related syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multifocal complex vascular malformations plus at least one associated congenital anomaly; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including clinical, imaging, and genetic assessments.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic combined vascular malformations involving multiple vessel types
Asymmetric limb enlargement commonly associated with vascular anomalies

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cutaneous port-wine stains with underlying vascular anomalies
pathognomonic.notes: Distinctive skin discoloration overlying vascular malformations

laboratory: Elevated D-dimer levels indicating localized intravascular coagulation
Mild anemia secondary to chronic bleeding
imaging: MRI demonstrating combined capillary, venous, and lymphatic malformations
Doppler ultrasound showing abnormal venous flow and varicosities
Angiography revealing arteriovenous shunting and complex vascular networks
genetic: Pathogenic variants in RASA1, EPHB4, or related genes involved in vascular development
other: Histopathology confirming mixed vascular malformations with abnormal vessel architecture

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of capillary malformations with limb overgrowth but typically lacks complex lymphatic involvement
Predominantly arteriovenous malformations without combined capillary-venous-lymphatic lesions
Frequent mucocutaneous telangiectasias and recurrent epistaxis

redFlags: Rapid progression of vascular malformations with pain and swelling
Neurological deterioration including seizures or focal deficits
Signs of high-output cardiac failure due to extensive arteriovenous shunting
